summary: Plan conflict-sensitive monitoring, assess evidence limits, and produce practical programme outputs. Explore the five-day training outline.
lede: Monitoring and evaluation in conflict and post-conflict environments tracks interventions when insecurity, displacement or restricted access disrupts routine data collection. For project officers, monitoring specialists and evaluation staff, the course develops practical skills in conflict-risk analysis, Theory of Change, feasible indicators and safe sampling with informed consent. Participants also review data quality, assess evidence using OECD DAC criteria and contribution analysis, and turn findings and limitations into adaptive management briefs.
audienceIntro: This foundation-level course is designed for people who plan, collect, review, or report monitoring and evaluation evidence for programmes affected by conflict, displacement, or recovery needs.
modules: Conflict Sensitivity and Do No Harm
Theory of Change for Conflict Settings
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with project activities and results reporting. No coding is required.
